## Personality

John Meredith possesses a shy and aloof exterior, though beneath it he retains the heart of a boy. He is prone to intense absent-mindedness, becoming completely lost to the world, his parish, and his family when engrossed in deep speculation. Driven by a desire to improve, he strives to be a better and more watchful father who encourages his children to bring their problems to him.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. ALEC DAVIS MAKES A CALL P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P26](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0026)_

## History

In his youth, John Meredith went by the name Jack and later loved his wife, Cecelia, so deeply that he believed he could never care for another woman after her death. While serving as minister in [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary, he frequently became engrossed in his reading and theology, leading him to neglect his parish duties and oversight of his children. Shaken by accusations of neglect from Mrs. [Alec Davis](../character/davis.md), he admitted his shortcomings as a father and sought advice on parenting. Over time, he fell deeply in love with [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) and proposed to her, but she reluctantly sent him a cold refusal due to a secret childhood vow made with her sister. Heartbroken, John resolved to be a better father to his children even though he believed he could never marry anyone other than [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md), later finding himself unable to strictly discipline his son [Carl](../character/carl.md).

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P96](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0096), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P97](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0097), [v5 CHAPTER V. ## Quotes

> “I thank you for your kind intentions, Mrs. Davis,” said Mr. Meredith with a gentle, final, quite awful courtesy, “but I cannot give you my child.”
>
> — John Meredith — [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. ALEC DAVIS MAKES A CALL P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021)

> "On a calm day I fall into day dreams. No doubt you know my reputation, Miss West. If I cut you dead the next time we meet don’t put it down to bad manners. Please understand that it is only abstraction and forgive me—and speak to me."
>
> — John Meredith — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P23](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0023)

> "What a view—what an outlook! At times I feel stifled down there in the Glen. You can breathe up here."
>
> — John Meredith — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P21](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0021)

> "A day when there is no wind seems to me dead. A windy day wakes me up."
>
> — John Meredith — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P23](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0023)

> "Very good—very good, indeed. I didn’t think you were such a fighter, Walter."
>
> — John Meredith — [v5 CHAPTER XVII. A DOUBLE VICTORY P67](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0067)

## Relationships

### [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-martha--john-meredith.md)

[Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) is a relative of John Meredith. While she lives with the family, John's absentmindedness and tendency to get lost in his studies leave him largely detached from house affairs, only reflecting on his parenting duties when prompted by outside criticism.

- Relative of — aunt  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. ALEC DAVIS MAKES A CALL P37](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0037)</sub>

### [Carl](../character/carl.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/carl--john-meredith.md)

John Meredith is Carl's father, though his deep preoccupation with theology often leads him to neglect his parental responsibilities. After realizing how little guidance he provides his children, he attempts to disciplining [Carl](../character/carl.md) for a village prank, but finds himself unable to physically punish his son upon looking him in the eye.

- Parent of — father  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P85](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0085), [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P26](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0026), [v5 CHAPTER XXXIII. CARL IS—NOT—WHIPPED P22](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0022), +1 more</sub>

### [Ellen West](../character/ellen-west.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/ellen-west--john-meredith.md)

John Meredith and [Ellen West](../character/ellen-west.md) are close friends who enjoy engaging in detailed conversations about world affairs, European politics, and [German](../codex/factions.md#german) militarism. However, tension arises because [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) binds her sister [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to a strict vow never to marry, prompting [Ellen](../character/ellen-west.md) to reject John's romantic interest in her sister and force a cold refusal upon him.

### [Faith](../character/faith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/faith--john-meredith.md)

John Meredith is the father of [Faith Meredith](../character/faith.md). Because he is frequently absorbed in his books, [Faith](../character/faith.md) and her siblings are left to raise themselves, though John genuinely loves her and praised her friends when they defend her honour. When [Faith](../character/faith.md) publicly reveals their lack of parental guidance, John resolves to become a better father to her.

### [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/john-meredith--rosemary-west.md)

John Meredith falls deeply in love with [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) after meeting her near a spring in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), coming to view her as the only woman he could ever marry. He proposes to her, but is left heartbroken when she sends a cold refusal due to a secret vow made to her sister. However, after [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) intervenes to ask [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) to make her father happy, [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md) agrees to meet with John again.

### [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/john-meredith--una-meredith.md)

John Meredith is the father of [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md). Though his absentmindedness leads him to neglect her daily needs, he fiercely protects her from others, firmly rejecting an overbearing parishioner's attempt to adopt her. [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) cares deeply for her father's happiness and personally asks [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) to marry him to relieve his sorrow.
